output.headline: Accepts Teach for America's free teacher training and summer school at Roosevelt Middle School
output.summary: Teach for America will provide five weeks of teacher training, including four weeks of teaching summer school, at Roosevelt Middle School at no cost to the district. Content areas include elementary reading, writing and math, and secondary English language arts, math and science. The memorandum of understanding runs January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2021.

output.headline: Pays a contractor up to $18,000 to help close the district's 2018-19 books and audit

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $18,000.00

output.summary: The district is hiring an outside professional for August 1 through October 31, 2019, at no more than $18,000. The contractor will support the 2018-19 unaudited year-end financial figures and the 2018-19 audit, process payroll, and guide accounting staff through closing tasks and entries. The work is overseen by the Chief Systems and Services Officer.

output.headline: Accepts free gardening classes for Thornhill Elementary students through 2022
output.summary: A community provider will teach a series of gardening classes at Thornhill Elementary School at no cost to the district. Students get hands-on learning of biology and ecology and learn about food sources and how to care for them. The memorandum of understanding runs August 12, 2019 through August 12, 2022.

output.headline: Approves up to $66,200 for safety and youth development services for newcomer students

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $66,200.00

output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract of up to $66,200 for safety intervention and youth development services for newcomer students, run through the English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department. The contract period is August 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, so it began before this approval.

output.headline: Accepts free Cazadero Performing Arts Camp music camps for middle school students through 2022
output.summary: Cazadero Performing Arts Camp will offer its outdoor music camps, "Jump Start In Music" and "Summer Music Camp," to participating middle school music students, with high school student mentors helping, at no cost to the district. The agreement covers September 15, 2019 through September 15, 2022.

output.headline: Approves up to $65,000 for Syntex Global translators for special education meetings

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $65,000.00

output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract of up to $65,000 with Syntex Global for extra translators in Arabic, Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese, Cambodian and other languages when district staff translators are not enough. The services include interpreting and translating legally required for Individualized Education Program (IEP) meetings. The term is July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, so it began before this approval.

output.headline: Pays Adkinstrak Timing Associates up to $6,000 to time track and cross country meets

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $6,000.00

output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract of up to $6,000 for customized timing services at track and field and cross country meets for students, through the Oakland Athletic League. The contract runs September 2, 2019 through May 27, 2020, so it began before this approval.

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $30,000 for coaching, mentoring and counseling at Horace Mann Elementary
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract of up to $30,000 with HERO for a coach who leads organized games and physical activities, the Young Hero Leadership Program for upper grade students, and counseling and mentoring at Horace Mann Elementary School. The contract runs August 12, 2019 through May 28, 2020, so it began before this approval.

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $27,000 for mentoring, PE and recess support at Garfield Elementary
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract of up to $27,000 with HERO for mentoring and leadership services at Garfield Elementary School, including a Young HERO leadership program for upper grade students twice a week, plus physical education and recess support for all grades. The contract runs September 3, 2019 through May 28, 2020, so it began before this approval.

output.headline: Pays HERO up to $30,000 for counseling and mentoring at Parker Elementary
output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract of up to $30,000 with HERO for counseling and mentoring at Parker Elementary School for Title I, Latino, African American and second language students. Services include social skills lessons, a leadership program, mentoring, professional development and organized recess. The contract runs August 12, 2019 through May 28, 2020, so it began before this approval.

output.headline: Awards Shah Kawasaki Architects $3,500,000 to design the Cole Administration Center project
output.summary: The Board is awarding an architectural services contract to Shah Kawasaki Architects for the Cole Administration Center Project, for up to $3,500,000. Work is scheduled to begin September 12, 2019 and last until December 31, 2022. The Board President and Secretary are authorized to sign the agreement.

output.headline: Adds $7,537.62 for Star Elevator's emergency repairs to McClymonds High School's elevator

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $7,537.62

output.summary: This amendment adds $7,537.62 to an existing contract with Star Elevator for emergency repairs to the passenger elevator at McClymonds High School, raising the contract limit from $34,688.90 to $42,226.52. The contract term runs from March 14, 2019 through December 31, 2019. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Pays First Alarm Security & Patrol up to $165,000 for alarm response when district police are off duty

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $165,000.00

output.summary: The Board is approving a contract of up to $165,000 for First Alarm Security & Patrol to respond to alarms and monitor sites when district police officers are off duty, including holidays and weekends. The term is July 22, 2019 through June 30, 2020, so it began before this approval.

output.headline: Passes up to $450,000 in child care funding to the Spanish Speaking Unity Council

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $450,000.00

output.sourceIssueCandidate: The text says the $33,750 administrative fee is payable "by the City" to the District, but the subcontractor named is the Spanish Speaking Unity Council, not the City.
output.summary: The Board is authorizing a subcontract of up to $450,000 of the district's 2019-20 state child development funding to the Spanish Speaking Unity Council, a nonprofit child development agency, for the Early Childhood Education Department. The text also lists an administrative fee of $33,750 payable to the district. The term is July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Pays Board on Track up to $45,000 to support and train charter school board appointees

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $45,000.00

output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract of up to $45,000 with Board on Track to help the Office of Charter Schools appoint members to charter school boards, build video training modules for new appointees, and give selected boards a skills appraisal in June 2020. The term is July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020, so it began before this approval.

output.headline: Awards R.F. MacDonald $59,433 for the Castlemont High School boiler replacement, without bidding
output.summary: The Board is awarding R.F. MacDonald Company a $59,433 contract for the Castlemont High School boiler replacement. The item's title says the contract was not competitively bid. Work is scheduled from September 12, 2019 to December 31, 2019.

output.headline: Awards Alaniz Construction $37,212 for parking lot repairs at the Sankofa kitchen project, without bidding
output.summary: The Board is awarding Alaniz Construction a $37,212 contract for labor and materials to repair existing parking lot pavement for the Washington (Sankofa) Finishing Kitchen Project. The contract was not competitively bid. The work was scheduled for August 8 through August 10, 2019, before this meeting.

output.headline: Pays Rook Electric $20,950 for security equipment repairs and installation done in May 2019
output.summary: The Board is approving payment of $20,950 to Rook Electric for repairs and installation of security equipment, as described in attached invoices. The contract covers only work already performed from May 1 through May 17, 2019, and was awarded without competitive bidding.

output.headline: Passes up to $250,000 in child development funding to the City of Oakland for Head Start

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $250,000.00

output.summary: The Board is authorizing a subcontract of up to $250,000 of the district's 2019-20 state child development funding to the City of Oakland's Child Development Agency for the Head Start program. The City will pay the district an earned administrative fee of 7.5 percent of the contract amount. The term is July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts free after-school study sessions from Study Buddy at Redwood Heights Elementary
output.summary: Study Buddy will provide after-school study sessions at Redwood Heights Elementary School at no cost to the district. The sessions focus on math, reading and writing needs, with the provider, teachers and parents working together. The memorandum of understanding runs August 5, 2019 through August 5, 2022.

output.headline: Pays a contractor up to $25,000 to supervise counseling interns at Oakland International High

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $25,000.00

output.summary: The Board is ratifying a contract of up to $25,000 for a contractor to supervise counseling interns and attend student support team and partner meetings at Oakland International High School. The term is August 12, 2019 through June 30, 2020, so it began before this approval.

output.headline: Approves union release time for a teacher under a National Education Association grant
output.summary: This side letter agreement with the Oakland Education Association (OEA) covers the National Education Association Community Schools Grant and release time so a teacher can take part in union leadership, for July 1, 2019 through June 30, 2020. The side letter stays in effect through June 30, 2022. The text gives no dollar amount.

output.headline: Authorizes up to $22,000,000 for 2019-20 nonpublic school and agency special education services

money.evidence: in a cumulative amount not to exceed $22,000,000.00

output.summary: The Board is approving new master agreements and individual service agreements with nonpublic, nonsectarian schools and agencies that serve students in special education, with a combined limit of $22,000,000 for the 2019-20 fiscal year. These are outside schools and agencies the district pays when it cannot serve a student in its own programs.

output.headline: Extends SERP Institute's chemistry curriculum project to July 2020 under an $80,000 Koshland grant
output.summary: This amendment extends the agreement with the Strategic Education Research Partnership (SERP) Institute, which supports development of a year-long high school chemistry curriculum, from July 31, 2019 to July 31, 2020. The item also accepts the associated $80,000 grant award from the Koshland Foundation. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Moves the date for recognizing the district's 2019-2020 Teacher of the Year
output.summary: This resolution changes the date on which the Board will recognize the district's 2019-2020 Teacher of the Year. No money is involved.
